title: Calibration run pruning and delegated access for quant profiles
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a telemetry-driven pruning and delegated access flow for calibration job runs and artifacts in the Redwood Console. This ticket defines a policy-first orchestration layer: automated pruning (TTL + cost/accuracy heuristics), per-organization retention quotas, and run-level delegated permissions so teams can safely delegate archive/prune operations without granting broader project-level admin rights.
background: Calibration runs (FP8/INT8 sweeps) create large artifact sets: quant profiles, evaluation traces, checkpoints, and candidate model binaries. Customers and internal tenants report: 1) runaway storage costs from long-lived runs, 2) difficulty in reclaiming space without losing provenance, and 3) need for fine-grained delegation so SRE/infra can manage storage while product teams retain control of accuracy validation artifacts.
goals: Provide an automated pruning engine that can remove or cold-store calibration artifacts based on TTL, storage budget, and quality heuristics
Add delegated role that allows safe run/ artifact lifecycle operations (archive, prune, restore) without full project admin access
Expose retention previews and cost impact in Console prior to destructive actions
Preserve auditability: all prune/archive/restore actions must be auditable and reversable within retention windows
success_metrics: Reduce average per-customer calibration storage usage by 40% in first 90 days
Zero customer-reported accidental loss of primary-calibration artifacts after rollout
90% of archived artifacts retrievable within SLA during trial restores
constraints: Any automated prune must preserve canonical quant-profile artifacts associated with pinned model versions or active rollouts
Compliance customers may require longer immutable retention (per customer flags)
Console UI must surface cost delta calculation without adding >150ms page latency
proposed_design: 1) Introduce a pruning policy object (TTL days, storage_budget_bytes, keep_top_n_by_accuracy, exclude_tags) configurable via Console and API. 2) Pruning engine evaluates runs nightly using telemetry: artifact size, last-accessed, accuracy delta to baseline, and cost signals; it proposes actions (archive to cold/ delete) grouped by tenant. 3) Delegated role 'calibration-operator' with scoped permissions: list/rerun/archive/restore/prune on runs and artifacts but no ability to change project settings. 4) Soft-delete and archive: soft-delete marks artifact as hidden for UI and eligible for GC after a secondary TTL; archive moves artifact to cold storage with manifest for restore. 5) Audit log entry for each action with operator, run id, artifact id, reason and revert token. 6) Preview modal in Console showing action summary, estimated reclaimed bytes, and list of artifacts kept due to pinning or accuracy thresholds.
ui_changes: Add 'Retention' tab to calibration run detail page showing per-artifact lifecycle state, last-accessed, approximate cost impact and a 'Prune preview' workflow. Add 'Calibration operators' group in Settings -> Access with grant UI and explanation of delegated scope.
api_contracts: New endpoints: POST /api/v1/calibration/policies (create/update), GET /api/v1/calibration/policies (list), POST /api/v1/calibration/runs/:id/prune-preview, POST /api/v1/calibration/runs/:id/prune-apply, POST /api/v1/calibration/artifacts/:id/restore. Actions require 'calibration-operator' or admin scope. All endpoints return operation id for async tracing.
retention_policy_spec: Policy fields: 'ttl_days' (stringified int), 'storage_budget_bytes' (stringified int), 'keep_top_n_by_accuracy' (stringified int), 'exclude_tags' (comma-separated string), 'pin_labels' (comma-separated string). Default policy: ttl_days=90, storage_budget_bytes=0 (unbounded), keep_top_n_by_accuracy=3.
permissions_model: Introduce 'calibration-operator' role. Mapped RBAC: calibration-operator can 'read:runs', 'list:artifacts', 'prune:preview', 'prune:execute', 'archive', 'restore' but cannot modify project-level retention policy or billing settings. Console will map the role to a scoped service account for automation.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable pruning preview for 10% of orgs; no auto-apply. Phase 2: opt-in auto-prune for non-compliance orgs with default TTL=90. Phase 3: enable delegated operator role and enable archive-to-cold for enterprise customers. Monitor restore success and audit trail. Communication: release notes + migration guide for large calibration datasets.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can create/modify a pruning policy in Console and via API
Prune preview accurately lists artifacts that would be affected and shows reclaimed bytes and keep reasons
Calibration-operator role can execute prune/restore flows and corresponding audit events appear in audit log
Soft-delete + restore tested end-to-end: restore returns artifacts intact within 30 days
Auto-prune engine does not prune artifacts pinned to active rollouts or with 'pin' label
E2E smoke tests for API endpoints and console flows exist in CI
